unit.why: A single anecdote: a nobleman who swore to shoot the Besht fails to see him when they are in the same house, because the Besht can make himself invisible.

stories.start_quote: שמעתי מהרב דקהילתינו שפריץ א׳ הי׳ שונא לבעש״ט
stories.end_quote: כשרוצה אין רואין אותו אפייס אותו
stories.summary_en: A nobleman who vowed to shoot the Besht arrives at a fortress while the Besht is there, enters the same house and does not see him; the commissar concludes that the Besht can be unseen when he wishes, and decides to reconcile with him.

tags.why: The story turns on the Besht's dealings with a gentile nobleman and a commissar.

quotes: כשיראה את הבע״שט יהרוג אותו בקנה שרפה
tags.why: The nobleman is hostile to the Besht and threatens to kill him.

quotes: האדון הנ"ל רגז מאד על הבעש״ט
דיבר הקאמיסאר עם האדון מהבע״שט ורגז עליו
tags.why: The nobleman's rage against the Besht is stated twice.
The Besht is miraculously invisible to his enemy.

quotes: ונכנס גם הבעש״ט לבית ונפטר מהקאמיסער
tags.why: The Besht is shielded from the hostile nobleman's threat.
The tale is about escaping a hostile noble, though the person protected is the Besht himself.

quotes: הלא הוא הי׳ בכאן כשבא אדוני
כיוון שהוא איש כזה כשרוצה אין רואין אותו
tags.why: The nobleman learns afterwards that the Besht had been there, and the commissar realizes what his power is.
The tale is framed as told by the local rabbi.

missing_concepts: reconciliation of a hostile noble with the tzaddik (אפייס אותו)
